surface_summary: A complex jewel theft and smuggling case unfolds in London involving a stolen necklace, multiple parties with ambiguous loyalties, and a series of deceptions. The police and amateur detectives pursue the criminals, but the true mastermind cleverly conceals the jewels and manipulates events.
accepted_facts: Madame de Borria's necklace was stolen from her hotel room.
Harvey Grimm was found in possession of a necklace similar to the stolen one.
Paul Brodie is an amateur detective pursuing Jeremiah Sands, a notorious jewel thief.
The jewels have been recut and disguised to avoid detection.
inferred_conclusions: Harvey Grimm is the outright thief who stole the necklace from Madame de Borria.
Jeremiah Sands is currently in London and directly involved in the theft.
Henriette Brinnen is an innocent victim caught in the criminal activities.
mechanism_description: Harvey Grimm, under the alias Ed. Levy, acted as the skilled artisan who secretly recut and disguised the stolen jewels to prevent their identification. The Brinnen family pretended to be criminals to protect the true ownership of the jewels, using the theft narrative as a cover. Grimm cleverly concealed the genuine necklace separate from the fake one to mislead the police and orchestrated the recovery and sale of the jewels while evading capture.
delivery_path: The Brinnen family brought the jewels to Harvey Grimm for recutting and disposal.
Grimm mixed the recut jewels with common jewelry in the workshop to hide them.
A fake necklace was presented to the police while the real one was kept hidden.
Grimm used disguises and false alibis to avoid suspicion and detection.
The police arrested Grimm on suspicion but lacked conclusive evidence.
The Brinnen family testified to the jewels' true ownership and secret disposal.
Grimm was released after the case was resolved and the jewels returned.
outcome_result: Harvey Grimm is revealed as the mastermind behind the jewel smuggling and is ultimately exonerated when the true ownership and purpose of the jewels are disclosed.

false_assumption.statement: Harvey Grimm was the thief who stole Madame de Borria's necklace.
false_assumption.why_it_seems_reasonable: Grimm was found in possession of a necklace similar to the stolen one and was caught with tools for cutting jewels, making him appear guilty. The police and detective Brodie strongly suspected him.
false_assumption.what_it_hides: The necklace Grimm had was entrusted to him for secret disposal by the rightful owners, the Brinnen family, who pretended to be criminals to protect the jewels. Grimm was acting under their instructions, not as a thief.

supporting_points: Brodie was suspiciously present at many key scenes.
He aggressively pursued the suspects and made arrests.
His overzealousness and blunders suggested possible ulterior motives.
He was suspected of being involved in the theft or cover-up.
false_solution.the_one_flaw: Brodie lacked concrete evidence and was repeatedly outwitted by Grimm and the Brinnen family.

red_herrings.description: The appearance of the Yellow Eye diamond worn publicly by a stage performer suggested reckless exposure of stolen jewels.
red_herrings.innocent_explanation: The diamond was swapped with a worthless replica to mislead the police and protect the real jewel.

red_herrings.description: Jack Lovejoy, an American actor with German ties, was suspected of espionage and involvement in the jewel theft.
red_herrings.innocent_explanation: Lovejoy was under surveillance but was not involved in the jewel smuggling; he was expelled from the country for espionage unrelated to the theft.

closed_circle.rationale: All principal characters are connected through the jewel smuggling and theft, with no outsiders implicated; the mystery revolves around their interactions and movements within London.

discriminating_test.design: The test involves verifying the presence and handling of the real necklace versus the fake one in controlled environments, including police custody and hotel rooms. By tracking the necklace's location and comparing it with suspects' movements and alibis, the investigators can prove who had access to the genuine jewels and who only possessed replicas.
discriminating_test.knowledge_revealed: This test reveals that Harvey Grimm was entrusted with the real necklace and only possessed the fake one when confronted by the police, proving his role as a protector rather than a thief.
discriminating_test.pass_condition: The real necklace is found in Grimm's possession separate from the fake one held by the police, confirming his innocence of theft and his role in the secret disposal.

fair_play_explanation: The reader is given detailed accounts of the characters' movements, interactions, and the jewels' descriptions. Clues such as the switch of necklaces, the presence of tools for recutting jewels, and the testimonies of the Brinnen family are all presented. The false assumptions about Grimm's guilt and Brodie's suspicions are explicitly challenged, allowing attentive readers to deduce the true mechanism of the jewel smuggling and recovery.
